findings: The map sends parent edge j to the actual return label and every other parent edge to its retained old label. Injectivity follows by separating old/new labels and then using old-label injectivity. Its image excludes exactly the soft edge, and exhaustive enlarged-label classification proves every other enlarged edge comes from a parent edge.

The mapped edge always ends at the retained old successor k+1. The exact successor equality criterion includes l!=j: the old incoming endpoint at j is followed by the soft edge, whereas mapped parent j starts at the newborn. This records the split incidence and avoids a false blanket preservation of adjacency.

Every remote parent pair remains remote after mapping. The proof excludes equality by injectivity and both adjacency orientations by the exact successor criterion. It asserts only this forward implication; a parent adjacent pair can become remote across the inserted soft edge, as needed for the newborn incoming/return pair.

The point and direction formulas are for the actual enlarged tuple. Only mapped parent j changes: its start gains epsilon*q and its direction loses epsilon*q. For every real segment parameter t, the complete affine point equals the parent edgePoint plus (1-t) times epsilon*q. Thus the terminal endpoint is retained and the parameter orientation is unchanged.

The three zero-parameter theorems recover the exact parent starting point, direction, and every affine edgePoint, including mapped j. They do not presume child G1 or Generic at the duplicate-vertex zero tuple.

All declarations use only n nonzero, arbitrary j, q, epsilon and t, with explicit remoteness only where logically needed. This includes the full source n>=3 domain, n=3, and all cyclic seams without geometric, root or orientation narrowing.

The sole first-failure repair changes the linear_combination multiplier for the negative adjacency branch from -hp to hp. Full body comparison confirms that all definitions and theorem types are unchanged; the successful log has only the recorded standard foundational axioms.
limits: This group supplies correspondence, remoteness preservation and exact affine formulas. It does not itself prove convergence estimates, persistence or completeness of crossings, G2, a common chamber, order of visits or Gauss-word identities. The phrase uniform in the segment parameter describes an identity valid for every t; a uniform norm bound is not asserted here. Stronger fidelity approval and canonical integration remain pending.
